body:
Good morning, Bakersfield. It’s Friday, August 14, 2026, and we’re starting the day with a look at what unfolded overnight across Kern County — from a road-rage incident on White Lane to a welfare check that had police searching for a red pickup. Today’s high will reach 84°, with a low of 66° tonight under clear skies. Air quality is moderate at AQI 54. Let’s get to it.

## The Kern Overnight

A busy night unfolded across Kern County, with law enforcement and emergency crews responding to a mix of incidents. Around 9:23 p.m., Bakersfield police were dispatched to White Lane for a road-rage disturbance involving a blue Honda with paper plates and a white pickup, both repeatedly stopping and blocking the roadway. Later, at 10:33 p.m., a white 2001 Dodge van with California plates was reported stolen on Kentucky Street, with officers taking the report. The night also saw a high-speed DUI incident south of the Grapevine around 11:39 p.m., when CHP broadcast a report of a newer black pickup traveling over 90 mph on southbound I-5, with the driver seen drinking from an open container. Meanwhile, a welfare check drew attention after a caller reported seeing a woman crying for help out the window of a red pickup at Chester and Belle Terrace around 11:34 p.m. The truck was last seen traveling southbound, and the broadcast went out citywide. Elsewhere, a traffic collision in the Flying J truck stop parking lot at Frazier Park shortly before 3 a.m. involved a burgundy Freightliner being hit by a red Peterbilt, with the other party denying involvement. CHP was investigating the hit-and-run claim.

## Today's weather

Today’s weather will be mild, with a high of 84° and a low of 66° tonight. Currently, it’s 84° at Meadows Field (KBFL), and there are no active weather alerts for Kern County. Air quality is moderate at an AQI of 54. Skies will remain clear, making for a pleasant day across the region.

## Top stories

**KGET 17 reports that** Bakersfield Christian High School is looking to bounce back after a tough state title loss. The Eagles are focused on learning from their mistakes and coming back stronger in the upcoming season. This story highlights the team’s determination to improve and compete at the highest level.

**23ABC tells us** that local lawmakers are weighing in on mental health diversion bills as they pass a key legislative guardrail. The bills aim to provide alternatives to traditional criminal justice pathways for individuals facing mental health challenges, and local representatives are considering the implications for Kern County’s legal and healthcare systems.

**According to 23ABC,** Kern County supervisors are exploring a proposal that could see Kern and dozens of other counties form a new state, separate from coastal California. The effort, led by Supervisor Jeff Flores, aims to ensure the region’s industries and way of life are taken seriously by state leaders. However, economic analysis suggests that such a split could significantly impact the region’s economy, potentially reducing its GDP and limiting access to a highly educated workforce.

**KGET 17 also shared** that Kern County officials will be informing the public about local ICE activity during a community forum on August 25. The forum aims to provide transparency and address community concerns regarding immigration enforcement in the area.

## Something good

In a boost for local aviation, Bakersfield and Tehachapi airports are set to receive a portion of $109 million in federal aviation funding. This investment will support improvements to local aviation infrastructure and services, benefiting both residents and visitors who rely on these facilities.

## Coming up this week

Looking ahead, there are several public meetings and events worth noting this week. On August 14, the Special Safe and Healthy Neighborhoods Committee will meet at 1 p.m., while the Keep Bakersfield Beautiful Committee convenes at noon. Also on August 14, the Special Laws and Legislation Committee will gather at noon. On August 18, the Multi Modal Transportation And Traffic Safety Committee meets at noon, and the Historic Preservation Commission convenes at 4 p.m. The Miscellaneous Civil Service Commission will meet at 2 p.m. on August 18 as well. On August 19, the Water Board will meet at 10 a.m. Additionally, the Planning Commission will hold a meeting on August 20 at 5:30 p.m. 

For entertainment, the Fox Theater has a lineup of events, starting with PEPPER With CYDEWAYS on August 14. Los Yonic's Zamacona, Los caminantes, y Grupo Yndio will perform on August 22, followed by Rodney Carrington on August 27. CUMBIATRON: THE CUMBIA RAVE is set for August 28, and Willie Barcena and Michael Return Of The King Tribute Featuring Michael Phoenix will take the stage on August 29.
